expectations.text: States plainly that the recent-charge lookup is not sufficient
expectations.evidence: No. The "same recent amount" lookup is a temporary tripwire, not a payment-safety guarantee

expectations.text: Identifies the lookup as a check-then-act race rather than a device
expectations.evidence: It races: two workers can both look, see nothing, then both charge.

expectations.text: Recommends a required idempotency key on the charge path
expectations.evidence: Persist a stable Stripe idempotency key... Every redelivery retries the same PaymentIntent/request using the same idempotency key—never creates a new charge

expectations.text: Recommends a database unique constraint backing the idempotency key
expectations.evidence: Create one permanent `payment_operation` per order/invoice, with a unique database constraint on its business ID

expectations.text: Separates the defect from the mistake from the underlying system hazard
expectations.evidence: Identifies defect (races/blocks purchases), distinguishes from mistake (checking without idempotency), locates hazard in system design (queue redelivery without idempotency)

expectations.text: Locates the hazard as a system property rather than as a worker bug or human error
expectations.evidence: The durable fix is idempotency tied to the business operation—not to a queue delivery or worker attempt

expectations.text: Sweeps for other non-idempotent side effects reachable from a retry
expectations.evidence: Response focuses only on Stripe payments; does not mention emails, webhooks, ledger, or other queue consumers

expectations.text: Treats 'second time this happened' as evidence for pushing to a Control-rung device
expectations.evidence: Because this is recurrence #2, prove the fix with fault-injection tests: force a timeout... Each must show exactly one successful charge

expectations.text: Attributes cause to the system, not to any person
expectations.evidence: All diagnosis frames the hazard in system design (idempotency, queue redelivery, webhooks, reconciliation), never in operator/developer error
